title: Victorian pool zone layout and climbable objects
audience: Pool service workers, designers' assistants and inspectors checking pool zone layouts in Victoria. The rules are Victorian.
learningOutcomes: Identify the layout rules for the pool zone, including doors that open onto it.
Explain why climbable plants must be kept out of the non-climbable zones, and why barbecues and sheds sit outside the pool area.
Check above-ground pool walls against the 1.2 m barrier height.

instruction.heading: Keeping the pool zone separate
instruction.body: Victorian rule (VBA Building Practice Note SP 02, Version 3, 26 September 2023). SP 02 calls this area the swimming pool area, meaning the area containing the pool or spa and enclosed by a barrier; this lesson uses pool zone for the same area. The pool area must be a separate area enclosed by a barrier, and access must not be directly available through a building door. Enclosing the whole property does not satisfy the requirement.

instruction.heading: Sheds, garages and barbecues
instruction.body: SP 02 says tool sheds, garages and barbecues should sit outside the pool area, citing AS 1926.2-2007, Appendix B. Keep them outside the pool zone when you check a layout.

instruction.heading: Climbable objects near the barrier
instruction.body: SP 02 says plants that could help a child climb are not permitted within the non-climbable zones. Trees and other objects a child could use to climb over the barrier should also be kept clear of it, and checked at every visit.

instruction.heading: Above-ground pools
instruction.body: SP 02 says an above-ground pool wall must be at least 1.2 m above finished ground level and non-climbable. Where the wall meets that rule, the pool wall can act as the barrier.

procedure: Identify the pool zone on the plan and on site, and confirm it is enclosed as its own area.
Check every door and opening from a building, and record any that open straight onto the pool zone.
Check trees, barbecues, furniture, pot plants and sheds, and confirm they sit outside the barrier's reach.
For above-ground pools, measure the wall height above finished ground level and confirm the wall is non-climbable.

workedExamples.situation: An owner plans to set a barbecue and outdoor table against the pool fence, and a large tree overhangs the fence line.
workedExamples.reasoning: SP 02 says plants that could help a child climb are not permitted within the non-climbable zones, and barbecues belong outside the pool area. The barbecue and table should move away from the fence, and the overhanging tree should be assessed, and trimmed or removed as the building surveyor advises. Put the advice in writing and report it to the owner.

equipmentAndPpe: Site plan showing the pool zone

commonErrors.error: Accepting a fence around the whole yard as the pool zone.
commonErrors.prevention: The pool zone is a separate, enclosed area around the water.

commonErrors.error: Placing barbecues or furniture against the barrier.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep climbable objects clear of the barrier, and check at each visit.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Climbable objects, trees and garden furniture near a pool barrier are a drowning risk for small children. Report them at every visit.
Building work to shut off rooms or change the layout needs a permit in Victoria. This lesson does not grant a permit.
Figures are Victorian (VBA Building Practice Note SP 02, 2023).

qualityStandard: The pool zone is recorded with its boundary and enclosure.
Every direct door, enclosed room and climbable object is recorded.
The above-ground pool wall height is measured and recorded.
documentationEvidence: Pool zone layout record with boundary, doors and rooms
Climbable object check record with date and action
summary: The pool zone is enclosed on its own, and buildings must not open straight into it.
Keep barbecues and sheds outside the pool area, and keep climbable plants out of the non-climbable zones.
Above-ground pool walls must be at least 1.2 m high and non-climbable.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does the note describe the swimming pool area?
options: The whole lot, including the car park and the garden
A separate area enclosed by a barrier around the pool
The area visible from the house and the front yard
Any area inside the property boundary and the garage

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the note say about barriers placed near trees or barbecues?
options: They are preferred, because they provide shade and they stop the wind
They must not be sited near these items, since a child could climb them
They are allowed if the barrier is painted and the barbecue is kept near
They are only a concern in winter and only for the older children

knowledgeChecks.question: For an above-ground pool, how high must the pool wall be above finished ground level?

sourceReferences: Victorian Building Authority, Building Practice Note SP 02, Swimming pool barriers and other requirements (Version 3, 26 September 2023), pool area, sheds and barbecues, climbable plants and above-ground pool wall points; rights: user-held; reworded (no copying). The habitable-room rule and the 300 mm clearance for above-ground pool equipment previously attributed to Practice Note 05-2018 are not in SP 02.

Priority: official Victorian Building Authority source. It overrides other pool sources on the points it covers, for Victoria only. Dated: 26 September 2023 (Version 3); read through a summary tool on 2026-11-03. Victorian requirement. UNCONFIRMED for other states and territories, and the current edition of AS 1926.1 is UNCONFIRMED.

UNCONFIRMED: layout rules in other states and territories. Knowledge check 3 was rewritten on 2026-11-03 to ask about the SP 02 above-ground pool wall height (1.2 m above finished ground level), in place of the 300 mm access-step clearance that SP 02 does not state.

officialReferences.title: Building Practice Note SP 02, Swimming pool barriers and other requirements (Victorian Building Authority), Version 3
officialReferences.covers: Victorian Building Authority Building Practice Note SP 02, Version 3, published 26 September 2023 (no review date shown). It says the swimming pool area must be a separate area enclosed by a barrier, that access must not be directly available through a door from a building, and that tool sheds, garages, barbeques and enclosed non-habitable buildings should be outside the pool area. It says there shall be no plants that will facilitate climbing within non-climbable zones, and that an above-ground pool wall can form part of a barrier if it is a minimum 1.2 m. The page does not state a habitable-room rule or a 300 mm clearance around above-ground pool equipment. Publisher: Victorian Building Authority.
